title: Power chords
summary: Two-note chords that drive rock, punk, and metal.

steps.title: What's a power chord?
steps.body: A power chord is a 'root + 5th' -- a perfect fifth (7 semitones) above the root. Because there's no third, it isn't major or minor. That ambiguity is exactly why it sits well over distorted amps: a major or minor third would clash with the harmonic mush; a fifth doesn't.

steps.title: E5 (open)
steps.body: The open low E + the 2nd fret of A. Just two strings rung out -- mute the rest with your strumming hand.

steps.title: A5 at fret 5
steps.body: Same shape, moved up. Root on the 5th-string 5th fret, fifth on the 4th-string 7th fret. This is the canonical movable power chord.

steps.title: Why a perfect 5th?
steps.body: The interval ratio of a perfect 5th is 3:2 -- the second-most consonant interval after the octave. Two notes a 5th apart reinforce each other harmonically; ramp up the gain and they sound like one big bell instead of two clashing tones.
